ghx vs raw gh on this machine
Before ghx: 3 sessions · After ghx: 3 sessions (acme, Opus 5.5)

Main thread          First try, before → after    Median cost, before → after
Check PR/CI status   100% → 100%  same            $0.027 → $0.027  same

Too few tasks to compare: Diagnose a CI failure; Create a PR; Merge a PR; Wait for CI; Whole PR,
  create to merge.
first try = the first attempt at the task worked: no agent mistake and nothing denied, up to and
  including its first command of that kind (a dry run counts); for a whole PR, none anywhere in it.
  Red CI or a busy run is not a miss.
cost = API spend for one task, as if each agent in it started from a 50k-token context.
better/worse = a clear difference; same = no clear change; too few = under 5 tasks on a side.

Failed GitHub commands, raw gh → ghx: agent mistakes 0.0% → 3.3% of commands (0 → 1, of them on a
  dry run 0 → 0); CI or PR state 0 → 0; refused by a hook, permission or the harness 0 → 0.

Biggest problems with ghx: none stand out clearly in this data.
Caveats: ghx data here is 3 sessions; across every repo, two sessions hold 82% of all ghx tasks, and
         two sessions hold 57% of all raw gh tasks.
         It compares the whole ghx setup (ghx, its hook, the CLAUDE.md block), not ghx alone.
Full report: pnpm eval   (pnpm eval --out DIR writes report.md and report.json)
